items.title: Nvidia opens inquiry after reports its CEO was targeted by spies
items.why: Nvidia’s board said on Sunday that independent directors will investigate reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The New York Times reported that US intelligence linked a Chinese businesswoman close to Huang to Beijing. Huang stays on as CEO.
items.matters: Nvidia makes most of the chips that power AI and is one of the world’s most valuable companies.

items.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ sets North American record for a foreign-language film
items.why: The Japanese monster film took an estimated $31.6m in the US and Canada over the weekend, topping the box office. AP and Variety say that is a record opening there for a film not in English, beating the $17.8m of China’s ‘Hero’.
items.matters: It is almost three times the opening of its predecessor, ‘Godzilla Minus One’.

items.title: Norris wins wet São Paulo Grand Prix as Mercedes take teams’ title
items.why: McLaren’s Lando Norris won a rain-hit race at Interlagos in Brazil on Sunday, 14.6 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen, with Isack Hadjar third. Mercedes secured the constructors’ championship, their ninth, with two races left.
items.matters: With Kimi Antonelli already drivers’ champion, Mercedes have won both 2026 titles.

items.title: Alcaraz beats Shelton to win the Paris Masters for the first time
items.why: Spain’s Carlos Alcaraz beat Ben Shelton of the US 7-6, 7-5 in Paris on Sunday, avenging his US Open defeat to him in September. It is his ninth Masters 1000 title and his fifth title of 2026.
items.matters: Alcaraz heads to the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, which start on 15 November.

items.title: Pope Leo tells Argentina the economy must serve people
items.why: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Buenos Aires on Sunday from Uruguay, the first papal visit to Argentina since 1987, and was welcomed by President Javier Milei. In his first speech he said the economy must serve the person, which France 24 describes as criticism of Milei’s austerity.
items.matters: Argentina is the home country of the late Pope Francis; Leo goes on to Peru on Wednesday.
items.changed: Updated: the pope has arrived in Argentina

items.title: UN climate talks open in Antalya, Turkey, with modest goals
items.why: Delegates meet in Antalya, Turkey, from Monday until 20 November for COP31, with world leaders due on 11 and 12 November. Talks focus on moving away from fossil fuels and on money for poorer countries. The US is not expected to attend.
items.matters: The UN says current national pledges put the world on course for about 2.6C of warming this century.

items.title: At least 34 killed as migrant boat sinks off Senegal
items.why: A wooden boat carrying migrants sank off Kebemer in north-western Senegal, between Dakar and Saint-Louis, at the weekend, killing at least 34 people, the state news agency APS says. The interior ministry says one person was rescued and others are missing.
items.matters: The Atlantic route from West Africa to Spain’s Canary Islands is one of the deadliest migration routes in the world.

items.title: At least seven killed in train collision near Cairo, Egypt
items.why: A train heading to Fayoum ran into the back of a Cairo-to-Aswan train in al-Ayyat, in Giza province south of Cairo, on Sunday afternoon. At least seven people were killed and more than 100 injured, Egypt’s health ministry says.
items.matters: President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi has ordered an urgent investigation into the cause.

items.title: NASA opens applications for new astronauts to staff a Moon base
items.why: NASA is taking applications for its next astronaut class until 3 December, it announced on Saturday at Kennedy Space Center in Florida. It has 32 active astronauts and plans a lasting base on the Moon. It expects to choose the class by late 2027.
items.matters: Applicants must be US citizens; the last call in 2024 drew more than 8,000 applications for ten places.

items.title: Cholesterol drug fails to prevent heart attacks despite cutting levels 78%
items.why: In a trial of 8,323 people in 42 countries, Novartis’s pelacarsen lowered lipoprotein(a), an inherited form of cholesterol, by 78%, but did not reduce heart attacks, strokes or heart deaths, researchers told the American Heart Association meeting in Chicago on Saturday.
items.matters: About one in five people carry high lipoprotein(a); several similar drugs are still in trials.

items.title: US sets up task force to block Iran's land supply routes
items.why: US Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate on Saturday to stop weapons and sanctioned goods crossing Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. The same day, it says, a US aircraft disabled a St Kitts-flagged cargo ship trying to break its naval blockade in the Gulf of Oman.
items.matters: It extends a months-long US naval blockade of Iranian ports to Iran's land borders.

items.changed: Updated: police raised the toll to at least six; the prime minister calls it terrorism
items.title: At least six killed in Krakow shooting, which Poland's PM calls terrorism
items.why: A gunman fired from a car in the Main Market Square of Krakow, Poland, on Saturday afternoon, killing at least six people and wounding about 15, police say. Officers shot and detained the suspect, a Polish man; three more bodies were found at his home.
items.matters: The interior minister says the suspect held ultra-nationalist views; Poland has declared two days of mourning.

items.title: Five killed as rain floods tens of thousands of Gaza tents
items.why: A sand embankment collapsed onto tents at a shelter south of Deir el-Balah in central Gaza on Sunday, killing at least five people, including children, Gaza’s civil defence says. Rain since Friday has flooded about 70,000 tents, the Hamas-run government media office says.
items.matters: Local officials and aid groups say Gaza urgently needs shelter, tents and heating as winter begins.
items.changed: Updated: at least five people were killed when an embankment collapsed onto tents

items.title: New Zealand beat Tonga 34-10 to reach Rugby League World Cup final
items.why: New Zealand's Kiwis beat Tonga 34-10 in Newcastle, Australia, on Saturday, after trailing 10-6 in the first half. It is their first World Cup final since 2013. They will play Australia or Samoa in Brisbane next Sunday.
items.matters: New Zealand's women's team, the Kiwi Ferns, also reached their final, beating Samoa 32-0.

items.title: New Zealand election too close to call after election-night count
items.why: With all polling places counted after Saturday's election, National has about 29.4% and Labour 29.2%, RNZ reports. National and its partners ACT and NZ First are projected to win a one-seat majority. About 700,000 special votes are still to be counted; final results are due on 27 November.
items.matters: The centrist Opportunity Party has entered parliament and could hold the balance of power.

items.title: Towhid Hridoy scores 242, Bangladesh's highest Test innings
items.why: Towhid Hridoy made 242 not out against West Indies in Sylhet, passing Mushfiqur Rahim's 219 not out from 2018. His innings took Bangladesh from 184 for 7 to 386, a first-innings lead over West Indies' 356.
items.matters: He is only the fourth Bangladesh batter to score a Test double century.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut to be first foreigner on China's space station
items.why: China's Manned Space Agency says a Pakistani astronaut will fly on the Shenzhou-24 mission as a payload specialist, Chinese state media reported on Saturday. The astronaut, not yet named, will make a short stay and return on Shenzhou-23. No launch date has been given.
items.matters: It would be the first time China's crewed space programme has flown a foreign astronaut.

items.title: Russian missiles hit Kyiv's power supply and a major bridge
items.why: Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles and 172 drones overnight into Saturday, mostly at Kyiv and the surrounding region, Ukraine says. Strikes damaged the Northern Bridge over the Dnipro and substations carrying power from two nuclear plants. Officials say at least one person was killed and several injured.
items.matters: It comes days before US-backed talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday.

items.changed: Updated: Eisenkot formally received the mandate on Sunday and says Likud could join
items.title: Eisenkot formally asked to form Israel’s government, open to Likud joining
items.why: President Isaac Herzog formally gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate in Jerusalem on Sunday. Eisenkot has 28 days, plus a possible two-week extension, to reach 61 of 120 seats; his alliance has 48 and Netanyahu’s bloc 53. He says Likud could join a government he leads.
items.matters: If he fails, Netanyahu could get a turn; if neither succeeds, Israel would vote again in the spring.
